Maya: quick heads-up — ran a full perf trace on dedicated A100 pool for the MoE routing regression. seeing repeated all-to-all saturation at token routing step, tail P99s up ~3x compared to baseline :warning:
Sam: rough numbers? is this across all model sizes or a specific variant?
Maya: observed on 1.2B and 7B configs. trace snapshot: repeated blocks where NCCL AllToAll occupies ~85% of step time, compute stalls while waiting for recv. microbatch size 8, expert fanout spikes to 128 for some batches.
Jonah: can you drop the flamegraph / trace link? and which kernel path was selected for FFN?
Maya: flamegraph https://perf.internal/redwood/jobs/1718204820 (internal). kernel selector picked grouped_gemm_v2 for FFN and quantized path for some layers. routing path is default noisy-topk. snippet from trace: ```
# timeline excerpt
[0.00s] dispatch routing
[0.03s] NCCL AllToAll start (fanout=128)
[0.18s] compute waiting on recvs
[0.21s] AllToAll end
```
Li: that pattern screams skewed expert distribution. did KV cache warmup change? skew could push many tokens to same few experts. we added smarter KV prefetch last week.
Maya: KV logs show heavy skew — ~62% of routed tokens hit the top 8% experts for this workload. looks correlated with recent batching heuristic change that pads up to larger microbatches.
Sam: we changed the batching heuristic to prefer larger microbatches for throughput on dedicated. that improves avg tokens/sec but can amplify peak fanout. maybe revert dynamic scaling? :thinking_face:
Jonah: immediate mitigation options: 1) cap per-expert fanout (e.g., max_fanout=64) 2) fallback to top-1 routing when hot_frac > threshold 3) enable NCCL async progress / background thread.
Maya: trying (1) locally reduced AllToAll time by ~30% in sim runs. patch idea: ```json
{"routing": {"max_fanout": 64, "overflow_policy": "route_to_dense"}}
```
Sam: note: overflow_policy needs to interact with batching logic — rerouting many tokens to dense increases compute. we should measure unit-cost tradeoff (tokens/sec vs cost-per-token).
Li: also add an observability metric: expert_hot_frac and per-expert-queue-length. throw an alert at 0.4 so we don't hit saturation silently.
perf-bot: queued perf job 1718204900 for canary (4 workers, 1000 seqs) — https://perf.internal/queue/1718204900 :eyes:
Jonah: I'll run the canary with max_fanout=64 + nccl async progress enabled and compare baseline. plan to run at 02:00 PT tonight. assigning to myself.
Maya: uploaded a small trace diff and opened PR #2345 (routing: cap + overflow->dense) and noted a potential bug in kernel selector where grouped_gemm_v2 is chosen even when quantized kernels are faster for the sequence length.
Sam: kernel selector heuristics were tweaked last month to prioritize fewer kernels; maybe the pruning logic forgot to check quantized benefit for short seqs. can you capture selector logs? (selector.debug=true)
Maya: pushed selector debug logs to the job artifacts. attached topologies and nccl info: `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows mixed NVLink/PCIe mesh on that pool which may amplify imbalance.
Jonah: good catch. mixed topology + skewed fanout => hotspots on links. adding a small random jitter to routing decisions could smooth peaks.
Li: for longer term: propose routing-aware batching heuristic — consider expert load when forming microbatches. not just tokens-per-batch.
Maya: agreed. short-term: canary tonight, enable max_fanout cap, collect expert_hot_frac and AllToAll latency traces. I'll post results tomorrow morning. tagging @oncall for visibility.
Sam: thanks. if canary looks good we can roll to dedicated pool with a 10% gradual rollout and an auto-fallback to previous routing config.
perf-bot: perf job 1718204900 completed: canary summary -> AllToAll p99 reduced 28%, tail latency down 18%, dense fallback increased compute by ~6% on hot batches.
Maya: awesome. created follow-up issue to extend batching heuristic and add metric dashboards. thanks team :thumbsup:
